bullets.title: Treasury Buybacks Fail to Hold: 30Y Yields Erase Gains, Rise to 5.25%
bullets.body: Wednesday's Treasury buyback announcement sparked a rally that completely unwound by Thursday afternoon, with the 30-year yield up 6bp to 5.25% and the 10-year breaking above 4.70%. JPMorgan and Goldman both warned the intervention is insufficient—fiscal concerns, not market structure, are driving long-end yields higher, and JPM forecasts a $3.5T+ funding gap requiring more duration supply, not less. Nomura called the buyback a 'band-aid on a bullet hole,' and Wolfe Research noted policy actions without fiscal consolidation risk fueling term premium further.

bullets.title: Bessent Signals Larger Buybacks, Activist Debt Management; Dismisses $40T Debt Alarm
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on CNBC that buybacks could exceed the initially announced $4B, that US yields don't reflect true economic fundamentals, and there is a 'very good chance' the fiscal deficit has peaked. He framed the $40T debt milestone as non-alarming—'we can grow our way out'—and pointed to incoming fiscal consolidation plans. Analysts remain skeptical: JPMorgan sees the move as credibility-risking without accompanying fiscal discipline.

bullets.title: Macro Data Solid: Philly Fed Posts Largest Monthly Jump Ever, Jobless Claims Beat
bullets.body: August Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index surged to 47.4 vs. 24.8 consensus—the largest monthly jump in the survey's 56-year history and the highest reading since August 1983. Initial jobless claims came in at 206k vs. 210k expected, reinforcing labor market resilience. The Conference Board Leading Economic Index also beat at +0.2% m/m vs. +0.1% estimate, reversing two months of prior declines.

bullets.title: US Equities Close Lower: S&P -0.87%, Nasdaq -1.00%; Retail and Semis Lead Decline
bullets.body: US equities finished lower Thursday with the S&P 500 down 0.87% and Nasdaq down 1.00%, led by weakness in retail (Walmart -9%, biggest drop since 2022 on slowest US comp growth in 6 years), banks, and semis. Energy and REITs outperformed. After-hours, S&P futures were effectively flat.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler CDS Blowing Out; ORCL and NVDA at All-Time Wide Credit Spreads
bullets.body: Post-July rally in AI-linked mega-caps appears to be fading, with hyperscaler CDS spreads widening sharply. ORCL and NVDA are reportedly at all-time wide credit spreads, and META is approaching record levels. Options flow confirms bearish near-term positioning: INTC and NVDA led most bearish options flow, and SPY saw millions of OTM put purchases at the open for the third consecutive session, with a $3.1B put wall at the 765 strike.

bullets.title: AI Capex Cycle Confirmed: JPM Sees $1.6T Revenue Run-Rate by End-2026, $1T+ CAPEX in 2027
bullets.body: JPMorgan calculates AI cloud, model providers, and neoclouds are on a combined ~$1.6T revenue run-rate by end-2026, growing 10-20% annually to $2.5-3T by 2030. Enterprise AI spending is estimated at ~$1.7T over next 12 months (5.8% of global expenses+capex). A separate projection pegs 2027 AI CAPEX above $1T ($661B compute, $300B data centers, $50B power). Token prices are down 40% while enterprise AI spending is up 50%, suggesting a Jevons Paradox dynamic.

bullets.title: Fed Officials: Data-Dependent, No Preset Bias; Musalem Flags Inflation Risk
bullets.body: Fed's Daly stated policy is 'in a good place' with no evidence calling for preemptive rate hikes and no signs of labor market faltering, while referencing Bernanke's 2004 approach as a possible framework shift toward more aggressive eventual action. Fed's Musalem was more hawkish, arguing 2% inflation is less likely at current rates, financial conditions are 'quite supportive,' and early hikes now could prevent stronger measures later. Prediction markets price 72% probability of no Fed change through December with zero cuts in 2026 at 86% probability.

bullets.title: Energy Surging: Oil Up 2-3%, Diesel $5.50+ National, Jet Fuel +76.5% YoY
bullets.body: WTI crude rose 2.9% to ~$88/barrel Thursday, with EU natural gas hitting 2023 crisis levels. US national average gasoline hit $4.10/gallon (a psychological headwind for low-end consumers per Walmart management), diesel above $5.50, California diesel at $7, and jet fuel +76.5% YoY. Bessent framed inflationary impulses as 'only from energy' and temporary, while macro funds remain bullish on oil despite administration rhetoric.

bullets.title: US Debt Crosses $40T; $658B Added Since July 1, Interest Costs Now Exceed $1T/Year
bullets.body: US national debt crossed $40 trillion for the first time, with the last $1 trillion added in just 152 days at a pace of $6.58B/day. Annual interest costs now exceed $1 trillion. Bessent acknowledged temporary deficit expansion from tariff refunds and pledged fiscal consolidation plans to be announced as early as next week.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Developing China-Specific Compliant AI Chip; Small-Batch Shipments by Year-End
bullets.body: NVIDIA is planning small-batch shipments of a new China-specific AI chip—described as an LPU (works alongside GPUs to accelerate processing)—designed to comply with US export controls, with several Chinese customers already placing orders. Beijing approval remains uncertain. Meanwhile, NVIDIA's first Vera Rubin racks are now powering OpenAI's training infrastructure, and Hudson River Trading signed a multi-billion compute deal with CoreWeave using Vera Rubin and HGX B200 GPUs.

bullets.title: 30-Year TIPS Auction: Yield 2.973% (Up 50bp), Strong Foreign Demand at 84.4%
bullets.body: The $8B 30-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.973%, up 50bp from the prior 2.473%, with the bid-cover ratio improving to 2.82 from 2.75. Indirect (foreign/institutional) bidders surged to 84.4% from 78.3%, while direct (retail) bids collapsed to 13.4% from 19.2%, suggesting foreign demand remains intact for US inflation-protected paper despite fiscal concerns.

bullets.title: Bessent on Iran: Maximum Economic Pressure, Press Conference Monday; Sanctions Expanded
bullets.body: Bessent signaled the US will 'collapse' the Iranian regime through economic warfare, calling it 'maximum economic pressure' with toughest sanctions yet and warnings to countries doing business with Iran. He stated military resumption is less likely under this pressure and sees all parties—including China—eager to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. A formal press conference on Iran plans is scheduled Monday.

bullets.title: Hedgeye August CPI Nowcast: +3.48% YoY, +12bp Acceleration on Middle East Energy
bullets.body: Hedgeye's August CPI nowcast projects +3.48% YoY headline inflation, up 12bps sequentially from the prior month, driven by Middle East energy market disruption. The official August CPI print is scheduled for September 11.

bullets.title: Bitcoin Surges Past $72K on Record Crypto Short Liquidations; Hedge Funds Net Long USD at 11-Week Low
bullets.body: Bitcoin futures rose 6.2%, moving above $72K on what was reported as the largest single-day crypto short liquidation in history. Separately, hedge funds remain net long the US dollar despite the greenback sliding to an 11-week low, creating a contrarian positioning dynamic.

bullets.title: WMT Consumer Signals: Low-End Pressured by Gas Prices Above $4, Wealthy Consumers Still Growing
bullets.body: Walmart's slowest US comp growth in 6 years (+2.6% ex-fuel vs. +3.5% estimate, impacted by pharmacy headwinds) triggered a 9% stock decline. Management attributed weakness to high gas prices above the $4 psychological level squeezing low-end consumers, while wealthier consumers continue to grow as a share. Citi restaurant traffic data corroborated: total footfall -2.7% YoY with QSR and fast casual decelerating, though CAVA remained strongest at +11.5%.

bullets.title: ERCOT Data Center Queue Frozen Pending Audit; Governor Abbott Halts Energization Approvals
bullets.body: Texas Governor Abbott is freezing ERCOT energization approvals for data centers pending an audit of the ~474 GW interconnection queue—approximately 5x the system's record peak demand and nearly all data centers. PUCT approved conditional Base Load notifications by August 31, with final audit verification delayed to December 10. HUT, CEG, and VST are expected to comply with quality standards; billions in collateral have been posted by developers.

bullets.title: AI IPO Wave Building: Anthropic Files by End of August at SpaceX-Record Valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic is set to file its S-1 as early as end of August, targeting a valuation that meets or exceeds SpaceX's record $86.2B IPO size. The company reported Q2 revenue of $11.5B with a $65B annualized run rate. The VC exit market more broadly is bifurcating sharply, with AI infrastructure and defense themes dominating IPO/M&A proceeds while traditional SaaS is severely underrepresented despite representing 50% of the unicorn backlog.

bullets.title: Gold Decoupling from Real Rates; Treasury Twist Viewed as Bullish for Gold and Equities by Some
bullets.body: Gold has stopped trading inversely to real interest rates, marking a regime shift that some analysts see as reflecting fiscal debasement risk. Mike Green characterized Bessent's long-end supply reduction strategy as designed to compress real rates, weaken the dollar, and lift both gold and equities, while Chris Wood argued the structural fiscal backdrop is more bullish for gold than stocks given $40T debt and potential Japanese repatriation pressure on Treasuries.

bullets.title: Labor Market Structural Risk: TPS Expirations Could Depress NFP to Near Zero or Negative
bullets.body: A JPMorgan analysis warns that TPS expiration for 400-500k workers from late July through early October will suppress NFP growth, potentially pushing the breakeven payroll pace (currently ~25k/month) to near zero or negative. Workers are concentrated in construction, transportation, and home health in Florida and Texas. Fed officials will struggle to distinguish this structural supply shock from cyclical demand weakness in fall labor data.

bullets.title: Data Center REIT Positioning: DLR and EQIX Among Largest Q2 Overweights; Towers Upgraded
bullets.body: Citi's REIT fund tracker shows data center REITs as the largest sector overweight in dedicated REIT funds at end of Q2, with DLR and AMT among the largest overweights by basis points. EQIX and IRM saw the largest sequential declines in ownership since March. Separately, Barclays upgraded both AMT and CCI to overweight on decade-low valuations and 2026 as a trough year, while Mizuho raised AMT's target to $208 on expected 2027 organic growth acceleration.
